claims.text: Raising the SPS sintering temperature to approximately 1000 °C will improve the heat-transfer capability of MgAlTiVFeCo-type high-entropy alloys.
SPS at 1000 °C produces greater densification and reduced porosity than SPS at 850–950 °C.
SPS at 1000 °C causes formation of a dense, continuous spinel-type oxide layer.
The oxide layer formed at 1000 °C is enriched in Al and Fe.
A continuous spinel-type oxide layer preserves structural integrity under high-temperature, high-heat-flux plasma-facing conditions.
The initial MgAlTiVFeCo alloy is produced by mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering at 850–950 °C.
MgAlTiVFeCo samples sintered at 850–950 °C have lower densification than samples sintered at 1000 °C.
MgAlTiVFeCo samples sintered at 850–950 °C have a less protective surface film than the 1000 °C sample.
Higher sintering temperature reduces grain-boundary scattering.
Greater densification enhances physical connectivity within the alloy.
Reduced grain-boundary scattering and enhanced physical connectivity increase thermal conductivity.
The protective oxide film changes corrosion to a diffusion-controlled process.
The 1000 °C-sintered alloy will have higher thermal conductivity than alloys sintered at 850–950 °C.
The 1000 °C-sintered alloy will maintain or improve mechanical strength relative to alloys sintered at 850–950 °C.
The 1000 °C-sintered alloy will have improved corrosion resistance relative to alloys sintered at 850–950 °C.
The predicted benefits will persist near 900 °C under the high heat flux and mechanical loading characteristic of plasma-facing reactor components.
Excessive oxidation or microstructural instability outside the proposed operating range could compromise performance.
Thermal transport properties were not directly measured in the cited study.

The hypothesis is falsified if the 1000 °C sample fails to achieve a statistically significant increase exceeding 10% in thermal conductivity while maintaining or improving mechanical and corrosion performance relative to 850–950 °C controls.
